liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Doll** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer finds China Doll deeply affecting, combining technical skill with emotional depth; Reviewer singles out China Doll as especially sweet [2][19][27]
- **Terrapin Station** (2 reviews): Bobby can faintly be heard calling for Terrapin a few seconds before it begins, after space; Bobby tells the band to start Terrapin as they come out of space [20][28]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Lovelight arrives unexpectedly; reviewer wonders whether it was spontaneous, and calls it inspired though not the best-played version; Reviewer clearly remembers Lovelight and thought it very good [20][22]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Not Fade Away starts hard, drops for Lovelight, then returns to finish the song; Not Fade Away, Lovelight and Not Fade Away made a fitting weekend closer, as Throwing Stones and NFA were rarely paired [25][28]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Minglewood in the first set is described as smoking hot [25]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review): Jerry's Dupree's solo is among the better ones of the era, with prominent wah effect [23]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 other source): Audience tapes lose about 20 seconds of the intro to tape flips; soundboard patch preserves Jerry's accents [2]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): Throwing Stones moves into Not Fade Away through a particularly striking transition [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-07-07.109750.beyer-senn-daweez.D5scott.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 144 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1984-07-07.165104.nak100.Reutelhuber.photoleon.flac2448**: source not stated; 20 songs; 146 min [2]
- **gd1984-07-07.sbd.miller.94379.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 134 min; rated 3.25/5 by 8 [6]. Said about its sound: Patch source was pitch corrected and remastered; the recording was very chopped up and hard to work with [6]
- **gd84-07-07.ziemba.connor.4861.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 135 min; rated 4.33/5 by 18 [7]. Said about its sound: Audience tape is not great, but likely captures the wah tones better than a soundboard would [23]
- **gd1984-07-07.163426.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 136 min [8]
- **gd84-07-07.set2-sbd.18752.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 13 songs; 89 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [17]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the transition works better on a good audience recording than on this matrix, though still trippy [24]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls a cold night, arriving late and missing Dire Wolf [22]
- A lawn ticket cost $10 and included overnight parking in the lot [22]
- From the 15th row, reviewer saw Bob speak into Jerry's mic by accident; Jerry shook his head at the crowd [26]
- Mud marked the run of shows at the venue [26]
- The parking lots at Alpine that summer had a heavily dosed scene [27]
- A friend named Kurt had called for Lovelight earlier that day, and it was then played [30]
- Uploader dedicates the tape to Sandy, nicknamed Bigfoot, a friend who had no part in the recording [1]
- Apart from Amsterdam and a New Year's show years earlier, first Lovelight by the band alone since Pigpen [20]
- Reviewer thinks only the 10-8-82 Dupree's solo might surpass this one [23]
- First set seemed short and weaker than the previous night's rocking show; the second set ripped [28]
- Reviewer ranks Alpine in the early 80s among the best places to see the band [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-07-07.109750.beyer-senn-daweez.D5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: source: 2 Beyer M160 & 1 Sennheiser 421 Microphones - 13th row-center > Nak MX100 w/2001 > Sony TC-D5M (Dolby on) - analog master cassettes; [1]. Also: Recording credited to Beyer and Senn mics, Da Weez and D5scott, transferred to 16-bit FLAC [1]
- **gd1984-07-07.165104.nak100.Reutelhuber.photoleon.flac2448**: taped by Bill Reutelhuber; transferred by Transfer by Anon Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel February 06, 2023; source: (Lawn, Spaced 10') Nakamichi 100 Shotguns > Sony TC-D5m > Master Cassette (TDK MA90s, Dolby B On) [2]. Also: Nakamichi 100 master from Bill Reutelhuber, with an anonymous transfer and soundboard and FOB patches from Robert Bryant [2]
- **gd1984-07-07.sbd.miller.94379.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Cassette -> Cassette -> PCM -> CD [6]. Also: Nakamichi 300 master cassette source patches the soundboard in Might As Well, Cold Rain, Playin', Drums and Not Fade Away [6]
- **gd84-07-07.ziemba.connor.4861.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steven Ziemba; transferred by CM>CDR>EAC(Secure Mode)>CDWave(Retracking Only)>shnv3(MKW ACT) by Charlie Connor; via Mike Lai & Jon Rianhard; source: Aud>Nak300>D5>CM [7]
- **gd1984-07-07.163426.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony D5M [8]
- **gd84-07-07.set2-sbd.18752.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBDMC(R?) > DAT > WAV > SHN w/ AUD(Senn 441s > D5 > DAT > CD) patches [17]

claims.text: Reviewer finds China Doll deeply affecting, combining technical skill with emotional depth
Bobby can faintly be heard calling for Terrapin a few seconds before it begins, after space
Lovelight arrives unexpectedly; reviewer wonders whether it was spontaneous, and calls it inspired though not the best-played version
Apart from Amsterdam and a New Year's show years earlier, first Lovelight by the band alone since Pigpen
Reviewer recalls a cold night, arriving late and missing Dire Wolf
A lawn ticket cost $10 and included overnight parking in the lot
Reviewer clearly remembers Lovelight and thought it very good
Jerry's Dupree's solo is among the better ones of the era, with prominent wah effect
Reviewer thinks only the 10-8-82 Dupree's solo might surpass this one
Audience tape is not great, but likely captures the wah tones better than a soundboard would
Throwing Stones moves into Not Fade Away through a particularly striking transition
Reviewer says the transition works better on a good audience recording than on this matrix, though still trippy
Minglewood in the first set is described as smoking hot
Not Fade Away starts hard, drops for Lovelight, then returns to finish the song
From the 15th row, reviewer saw Bob speak into Jerry's mic by accident; Jerry shook his head at the crowd
Mud marked the run of shows at the venue
Reviewer singles out China Doll as especially sweet
The parking lots at Alpine that summer had a heavily dosed scene
Bobby tells the band to start Terrapin as they come out of space
First set seemed short and weaker than the previous night's rocking show; the second set ripped
Not Fade Away, Lovelight and Not Fade Away made a fitting weekend closer, as Throwing Stones and NFA were rarely paired
A friend named Kurt had called for Lovelight earlier that day, and it was then played
Reviewer ranks Alpine in the early 80s among the best places to see the band
Recording credited to Beyer and Senn mics, Da Weez and D5scott, transferred to 16-bit FLAC
Uploader dedicates the tape to Sandy, nicknamed Bigfoot, a friend who had no part in the recording
Nakamichi 100 master from Bill Reutelhuber, with an anonymous transfer and soundboard and FOB patches from Robert Bryant
Audience tapes lose about 20 seconds of the intro to tape flips; soundboard patch preserves Jerry's accents
A few notes of Playin' in the Band are heard after China Doll
Nakamichi 300 master cassette source patches the soundboard in Might As Well, Cold Rain, Playin', Drums and Not Fade Away
Patch source was pitch corrected and remastered; the recording was very chopped up and hard to work with
Master cassette from Stephen Thomas, transferred by Charlie Miller, with a 49-second Drums patch from Stephen Ziemba's Nakamichi 300
